text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Valdas Adamkus, a 72-year-old Lithuanian-American and former E.P.A. bureaucrat, will run in the upcoming presidential elections for the Centre Union.
- Vilniaus Prekybos Mazhmena will control three out of four enterprises selling sugar, and consumers are worried that it will raise sugar prices.

- At the end of last week Tauras Bank shareholders said that they are initiating bankruptcy procedures. The fate of the estimated 59 to 70 enterprises that belonged to Lietverslo Corporation, which the late Tauras Bank president Genadijus Konopliovas was also head of, remains uncertain.
- Mazeikiu Nafta is earning a profit for the first time in five years. Its profit this year is 2.7 million litas so far, and the company earned 13.7 million litas in May.

- Lithuanian-American Valdas Adamkus, who was declared the presidential candidate of the Centre Union on Saturday, does not intend to join the party. He said that the head of state must be the "moral national authority."
- The World Bank is beginning a mission to Lithuania today that will end on July 11.

- The agriculture and forestry ministry has suggested raising minimum prices for producers of some types of milk by four Lithuanian cents per kilogram and to leave the state subsidy unchanged. How much and when prices will be raised will be announced today.

- The government decided on June 25 to abolish VAT advantages. The finance ministry said the change was necessary due to European directives, but Lithuania's tourism industry is worried that it will give advantages to foreign companies who do not pay VAT abroad.
- Lithuania's Inta will supply modern communications for Ignalina nuclear power plant. Sweden contributed $900,000 to the project.
